body:
Hi, thanks for the PR.

> Classes in GDScript that do not extend from Resource or from Node have no use for the `@export` annotation(s).

This is not correct. While the inspector is indeed mainly intended for Nodes and Resources, it does support editing Object classes. See the following screenshot, where I inspect a custom `Test` class which is inheriting `Object`, and the presence of `@export` does influence the outcome:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fa53c6e1-464a-41ea-9914-32bfe6d7202c)

This is extensively used by the engine, to inspect the editor/project settings, import/export settings, etc. but as you can see it is also available to scripting.

That sounds to me like something of an edge case scenario, or might be better implemented with a special annotation.

While you can make non-Nodes non-Resources *visible* in the inspector using tools, they cannot integrate with Godot's resource/export system, right? Like, I'm not sure what the use-case is for what you described?

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d09dc040-987d-46e5-8f28-9badbf6d44b6)

Exporting properties has two purposes: displaying the property in the editor and serializing it to a file. It is true that standard Godot scenes/resources only support two object classes: `Node` and `Resource` (plus their subtypes). However, this does not change the fact that property info is a system of the `Object` base class. Since you can use the same property hints and usage flags in `_get_property_list()` and `_validate_property()` for `Object`-derived classes, I see no reason why we should prohibit doing this via export annotations, which are essentially convenient shorthands to the same system.

As RedMser said above, you can edit `Object` instances in the inspector, and export hints can affect the appearance and behavior of editor fields, despite the fact that `PROPERTY_USAGE_STORAGE` has no effect. Especially if we add the ability to create custom inspectors in plugins in the future. It is also possible to implement custom serializers that can save/load objects that are not nodes or resources.

Finally, I don't think we should add warnings with inverse logic. We can't know in advance whether some other serializable object types will appear in the future, in addition to `Node` and `Resource`. For example, we might want to add support for collections (`Set`, `Queue`, etc.), but not implement them as `Variant` types.

You might argue that warnings are not errors, that users can disable or ignore them, and that we can deprecate the warning if necessary. True, but I'm still not sure this case deserves a dedicated warning, given the above. I don't recall ever seeing such a bug in my or other users' projects. We should mention this detail in the online documentation, but I don't think we should worry about it any more.
